- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended hiking spots close to Denver include:
  - Chautauqua Trail (Boulder): A popular trail with stunning views of the Flatirons and the Rocky Mountains. (30 minutes from Denver)
  - Mount Sanitas (Boulder): A moderate 3.1-mile hike with panoramic views of Boulder and the surrounding mountains. (30 minutes from Denver)
  - Lookout Mountain: A moderate 4.4-mile hike with spectacular views of the Great Plains and the Rockies. (30 minutes from Denver)
  - Dinosaur Ridge: A short, easy hike with dinosaur fossils and stunning views of the Rocky Mountains. (30 minutes from Denver)
  - Red Rocks Park and Amphitheatre: A short, easy hike with unique red rock formations and great views of Denver. (20 minutes from Denver)
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended hiking spots within 1-2 hours from Denver include:
  - Rocky Mountain National Park (Estes Park): Offers numerous trails for all levels, including the popular Bear Lake Trail and the challenging Keyhole Route to Longs Peak. (1 hour 15 minutes from Denver)
  - Maxwell Falls (Evergreen): A moderate 4-mile hike to a beautiful waterfall. (1 hour from Denver)
  - St. Mary's Glacier (Idledale): A moderate 3.5-mile hike to a picturesque glacier and alpine lake. (1 hour 15 minutes from Denver)
  - Grays Peak (Silver Plume): A challenging 8.5-mile hike to the highest point on the Continental Divide. (1 hour 30 minutes from Denver)
  - Georgetown Lake (Georgetown): A moderate 4-mile hike around a beautiful lake with stunning mountain views. (1 hour 15 minutes from Denver)

  - Always check the trail conditions and difficulty level before heading out.
  - Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and layers for changing weather conditions.
  - Be mindful of altitude sickness and take breaks if needed.
  - Respect wildlife and the environment, and follow any regulations or guidelines.
  - Consider downloading a hiking app or map to help navigate the trails.
